newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end bourse trade one percent higher.
newsitem.headline: German shares end bourse trade one percent higher.

text.p: German shares rose strongly in bourse trade on Wednesday as they sought to match gains registered in late electronic trade on Tuesday evening and ended the day one percent higher.

However, further significant gains were ruled out as market uncertainty over the Bonn/Bundesbank row over the revaluation of German assets continued to upset sentiment, despite soothing statements from both sides.
The DAX index of 30 blue-chip German stocks ended at 3,661.84 points, a rise of 36.10 points or one percent after what dealers said was a low volume session.
"The dollar is helping us this morning, and the debt market seems to be settling down a little bit too, which also helps," a Frankfurt trader said.
The dollar came off slightly at 1.7291/96 marks in early bourse.

In a series of statements over the morning, both Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said the German government and the Bundesbank had reached a way of proceeding on a planned revaluation of central bank assets.
He also said that he and Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer would do their best to have windfall funds created by the revaluation transferred to Bonn from 1998 and not earlier.
The decision had a fairly neutral effect on shares, despite the fact that uncertainty about the future of European currency union had translated into negative sentiment in the equity market of late.
Among winners in bourse trade was tyre-maker Continental AG, which ended off highs, up 50 pfennigs at 39.85 marks, having earlier hit 40.20 marks.

The German financial newsletter Platow Brief said Conti expected to report a distinct increase in 1997 profit at its annual meeting, which lifted the share earlier, while the group said at its annual meeting afterwards that it expected earnings to grow strongly in 1997.
Germany's large utilities were also higher early on, enjoying a cyclical upturn, although they pared gains as trade progressed.
Viag AG ended up 10.50 marks, or 1.33 percent, at 785.50 marks, while Veba was up 1.25 marks, or 1.27 percent at 98.60 marks.
Dollar strength also boosted car stocks, particularly Volkswagen AG, which rose 29 marks or 2.46 percent, to 1,175 marks.

Shares in Deutsche Telekom AG were higher after Wolfgang Schaeuble, parliamentary leader of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), said the sale of the government stake in the company would be done in a way that would not upset shares.
Telekom shares ended up 55 pfennigs, or 1.42 percent, at 38.90 marks.
Privatisation talk also boosted airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG which ended up 1.15 marks, or nearly four percent, at 29.50 marks.
